newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed, Northrop get $234.9 mln Army deal.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Northrop get $234.9 mln Army deal.

text.p: Longbow LLC, a joint venture between Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp said Monday it won a $234.9 million U.S. Army contract to make anti-armor missiles and missle launcheers.
In a so-called continued low-rate initial production deal, the Army contract calls for the production of more than 1,000 Longbow missiles and 200 launchers, it said.
The contract represents a significant "ramp-up" toward a full production contract anticipated next year, said Richard Russell, president of Longbow.

The Longbow system is an integrated fire control radar and missile system developed and built by the joint venture for the U.S. and British ground forces. The company said it started missile production in December 1995 while production of fire control radars began in March 1996.
It said the Longbow is designed to provide adverse weather "fire and forget" antiarmor targeting and attack capabilities for the two types of Apache attack helicopters.
In the future, RAH-66 Comanche light attack/scout helicopters will also carry them, it said.
